paragraphs.edited: When I was 15, I remember going to my mom and telling her that I was having a hard time seeing what was in front of me — I was having a hard time seeing the board. I didn't think much of it — I just didn't think much of it. But I realized that sitting in the back of class, where I like to sit, I couldn't see anything. Then it got serious when I started to drive and realized that there were signs I thought I should be able to see, or that my friends had told me about, that I wasn't seeing. Something wasn't right. So I went to the doctors — I went to the eye doctor — and they did all the little checks.

paragraphs.heading: What a worldview is
paragraphs.edited: We're talking about worldviews. The most simplistic way to see it and understand it is this: you look at the world through a set of lenses, and how you look through those lenses dictates how you see the world. Worldview — how I view the world. But worldviews are more than that, and what you should now start to see through the worldview questions that were introduced is that worldviews are foundational. They are life-shaping questions about reality. It's not just the pair of glasses I'm looking through to see the world; it's literally how I'm interpreting it and how I'm living as a result of that view. Your students should see very quickly, through some of the activities in the Bible study, that a biblical worldview has a profound impact on how we live.

paragraphs.heading: Change takes time
paragraphs.edited: And finally, don't expect students to change their worldview right away. Just because you see that they have a different worldview, or that they have inconsistencies in their worldview, or that there are some questions in their worldview, and you present the Christian worldview — even at the end of these 32 weeks — don't expect them to just go, "Oh, I'm going to put on a whole new pair of glasses and see the world totally differently." It doesn't work that way. In fact, it doesn't work that way at all. Changing how we see the world is not as easy as changing the prescription on a pair of glasses. It's a huge, huge adjustment.

paragraphs.heading: Three things to remember
paragraphs.edited: But remember, when we're talking about worldviews, the three things you need to keep in mind are these: your students may not necessarily have the biblical worldview that you think they have; their worldview needs to not be a buffet, but coherent and consistent; and don't expect them to change it right away. Be patient — and I think that's probably the most important piece, to be patient with them. Pray with them. Continue to walk alongside them to help them understand truth and how it fits in, and how truth is going to change their reality, and how understanding Scripture and their understanding of truth is going to actually change their worldview slowly, but also profoundly.
